A 1990s legend walks through Tokyo Tower’s portal again tonight.

A familiar fantasy returns to Japanese television on October 7. The surprising part is why a story born before smartphones may fit 2026 so well.

By Yuji Shimizu · YUJI @ Japan
October 7, 2026 · 5 min read

Tokyo Tower is one of those landmarks that seems impossible to separate from the city. Tonight, it becomes a doorway again.

Magic Knight Rayearth, the fantasy adventure created by CLAMP, begins a new television adaptation in Japan. Its premise remains irresistible: three schoolgirls visiting Tokyo Tower are pulled into another world and asked to become the legendary Magic Knights.

That setup helped the original 1990s series stand out by combining magical-girl emotion, role-playing-game structure and giant robots. For older viewers, the new version carries nostalgia. For younger viewers, it may feel strangely current.

The reveal is not simply that Rayearth is back. It is that one of anime’s early genre-mixing worlds is returning to an audience raised on games, quests and portal fantasies.

Why tonight matters

The fall anime calendar is crowded, but Rayearth arrives with something new productions cannot manufacture overnight: memory shared across generations. Parents who watched the earlier adaptation can now meet the same characters alongside viewers encountering Cephiro for the first time.

Tokyo before the fantasy

The story’s leap from Tokyo Tower matters. It begins with a real place, recognizable to visitors, and turns that place into the edge of another world. That movement—from Japanese landmark to adventure—is one reason the series remains easy to remember.

The new series is scheduled to begin on TV Asahi on October 7, with other broadcasts and streaming following. International availability may differ by region, so viewers should confirm local platforms.
